# Writer identification with a CNN (Task 2)

**Prediction task.** The input is a single 28 × 28 image, scaled to $[0,1]$; the response is the writer ID (20 classes). The digit is not given to the model. The CNN follows the Lecture 4 pattern (@tbl-cnn-arch), is trained with categorical cross-entropy and Adam (batch size 128), and stops early when validation loss has not improved for 5 epochs. A second version adds random rotation (up to about 15°), zoom and shift (up to 10%) to the training images.

| Layer | Output shape | Parameters |
|---|---|---|
| Conv 32 filters 3×3, ReLU | 26 × 26 × 32 | 320 |
| Conv 32 filters 3×3, ReLU | 24 × 24 × 32 | 9,248 |
| Max pool 2×2, dropout 0.25 | 12 × 12 × 32 | 0 |
| Conv 64 filters 3×3, ReLU | 10 × 10 × 64 | 18,496 |
| Max pool 2×2, dropout 0.25 | 5 × 5 × 64 | 0 |
| Flatten, dense 128 ReLU, dropout 0.5 | 128 | 204,928 |
| Dense 20, softmax | 20 | 2,580 |

: CNN architecture (`src/cnn.py`); `{python} f"{cnn_summary['n_params']:,}"` parameters in total. {#tbl-cnn-arch}

# Siamese network for writer matching (Task 3)

**Design.** A shared embedding CNN (same convolutional layers as @tbl-cnn-arch, then dense 128 and a 64-unit output scaled to length 1) maps each image to a vector. Training uses the triplet loss [@schroff2015facenet], following the Keras example in the course notes [@essam2021keras]:
$$
L(A,P,N) = \max\!\left(\lVert f(A)-f(P)\rVert^2 - \lVert f(A)-f(N)\rVert^2 + \alpha,\ 0\right), \qquad \alpha = 0.5 .
$$
Two images are declared to be by the same writer when the squared distance between their embeddings is below a threshold chosen on validation writers (`src/siamese.py`).

| Image | Writer | Digit | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anchor $A$ | random | random | random |
| Positive $P$ | same as $A$ | same as $A$ | different from $A$ |
| Negative $N$ | different from $A$ | same as $A$ | random |

: Construction of training triplets; 15,000 new random triplets are drawn every epoch. {#tbl-triplets}

[Explain why the digit is held fixed in every triplet and why positives come from a different session (link to the EDA).]

As a comparison, a second Siamese network with **contrastive loss** [@hadsell2006dimensionality] was implemented by Lehlonono Nkejane (originally in R; ported to Python in `src/contrastive.py`): a smaller encoder (16-dimensional embedding), one fixed set of 6,000 training pairs (same digit, different sessions, half same-writer), 10 epochs. Both models are evaluated on the same test pairs.

```{python}

#| output: asis
tab = pd.DataFrame({"Triplet Siamese": sia_main.set_index("fold").AUC,
                    "Contrastive Siamese": contrast.set_index("fold").AUC,
                    "Raw pixels": raw_main.set_index("fold").AUC})
tab.loc["mean"] = tab.mean(); tab.loc["sd"] = tab.iloc[:5].std()
show_table(tab, index=True)
```

# Hyperparameter sensitivity (Task 5)

The triplet margin (0.2, 0.5, 1.0) and the embedding size (16, 64) were varied for the Siamese network, trained on sessions 1–3 of all writers and scored on session 4 only. The default (0.5, 64) was repeated with three seeds to measure run-to-run variation.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-hpo
#| tbl-cap: "Validation results (session 4) for each setting. AUC: same-writer vs different-writer pairs of a session-4 and a session 1–3 image; identification: nearest-prototype accuracy over 20 writers."
#| output: asis
show_table(hpo[["margin", "embedding size", "seed", "epochs", "val AUC", "val EER",
                "val identification", "val top-3"]])
grid = hpo[hpo.seed == 0]
seeds = hpo[(hpo.margin == 0.5) & (hpo["embedding size"] == 64)]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hpo
#| fig-cap: "Sensitivity of validation AUC (left) and identification accuracy (right) to the triplet margin and embedding size. Grey band: range over three seeds of the default setting."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7, 2.8))
for ax, metric in zip(axes, ["val AUC", "val identification"]):
    for dim, g in grid.groupby("embedding size"):
        ax.plot(g.margin, g[metric], marker="o", ms=4, label=f"size {dim}")
    ax.axhspan(seeds[metric].min(), seeds[metric].max(), color="grey", alpha=0.2, label="seed range")
    ax.set_xticks([0.2, 0.5, 1.0]); ax.set_xlabel("margin"); ax.set_title(metric)
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Across the grid, validation AUC ranges from `{python} f3(grid["val AUC"].min())` to `{python} f3(grid["val AUC"].max())`; the three seeds of the default setting range from `{python} f3(seeds["val AUC"].min())` to `{python} f3(seeds["val AUC"].max())`. Identification accuracy ranges from `{python} f3(grid["val identification"].min())` to `{python} f3(grid["val identification"].max())` across the grid.

[Interpret: how sensitive each measure is relative to seed noise; which setting was chosen and why the choice is partly chance; limits of the search.]

# Comparison of the CNN and the Siamese network (Task 6)

Both models are compared on the session split (test = session 5). The Siamese network identifies writers by the nearest *prototype*, the average embedding of each writer × digit in sessions 1–3 [@snell2017prototypical; @utkin2019explanation]; the CNN's 128-unit feature layer is also used in the same way. For verification, a session-5 image is compared with a session 1–3 image of the same digit.

```{python}
#| label: fig-confusion
#| fig-cap: "Confusion matrix of the augmented CNN on session 5 (rows: true writer, normalised to sum to 1)."
#| fig-height: 4.5
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, pred_aug, normalize="true")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4.5))
im = ax.imshow(cm, cmap="Blues"); ax.grid(False)
ax.set_xticks(range(20), range(1, 21), fontsize=6); ax.set_yticks(range(20), range(1, 21), fontsize=6)
ax.set_xlabel("predicted writer"); ax.set_ylabel("true writer")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pca
#| fig-cap: "First two principal components of the images, coloured by digit (left) and by writer (right)."
Z, pca_share = eda.pca_2d(images)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7, 3))
axes[0].scatter(Z[:, 0], Z[:, 1], c=meta.digit, cmap="tab10", s=0.5, alpha=0.5)
axes[1].scatter(Z[:, 0], Z[:, 1], c=meta.person_id, cmap="tab20", s=0.5, alpha=0.5)
for ax, t in zip(axes, ["by digit", "by writer"]):
    ax.set_title(t); ax.set_xlabel("PC1"); ax.set_ylabel("PC2")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

The first two components explain `{python} f"{100 * pca_share:.0f}"`% of the pixel variance.
